delivery.postgres_client: node-postgres (pg) over a pooled binary socket
delivery.note: Each engine is driven through the client it provides. Sirannon runs over its SDK's default WebSocket transport, which multiplexes every concurrent request over one persistent socket, and PostgreSQL runs over node-postgres on its binary socket protocol, with one pooled connection for each request that the generator allows in flight. One Node load generator drives both, so the coordinated-omission instrument behaves identically for each. The load driver runs on its own machine and reaches the engine over the private network between the two machines, so every request crosses that network. The engine under test runs as a native process under a hard memory ceiling (cgroup v2) with every CPU of its machine, and it shares that machine with nothing but the harness.

operation_cost.note: One operation is one unit of offered load and one unit of the reported rate. Statements and round trips per operation are the weighted mean across this workload's operation mix. Round trips are a property of each engine's client, so a rate on a workload costing several round trips per operation is not comparable with a rate on a workload costing one.

engine_cpu.note: cores_used is the engine cgroup's cpu.stat usage divided by wall time over the measured span, so it is the average number of cores the engine kept busy, not a peak.

seed.note: Seeding is disclosed, never compared: each engine loads through its own fastest documented path, and Sirannon seeds with durability off while PostgreSQL seeds inside one transaction.

generator.note: offered_fraction is the share of the target rate the generator actually offered, and it is the field to read for whether the load was delivered. The generator keeps sending scheduled requests late while the engine falls behind, so offered_rate shows a shortfall through the elapsed time. It stops sending once one further measurement window has passed after the window ends, and missed_in_window counts the scheduled requests that it never sent; a pass with any missed request is not sustained. cap_occupancy is the fraction of the window, sampled off the request path, that the generator spent with its in-flight cap full; near one means requests were waiting on the server rather than on the generator, and occupancy_samples is how many samples that fraction rests on.

engine_cpu.note: cores_used is the engine cgroup's cpu.stat usage divided by wall time over the measured span, so it is the average number of cores the engine kept busy, not a peak.

generator.note: offered_fraction is the share of the target rate the generator actually offered, and it is the field to read for whether the load was delivered. The generator keeps sending scheduled requests late while the engine falls behind, so offered_rate shows a shortfall through the elapsed time. It stops sending once one further measurement window has passed after the window ends, and missed_in_window counts the scheduled requests that it never sent; a pass with any missed request is not sustained. cap_occupancy is the fraction of the window, sampled off the request path, that the generator spent with its in-flight cap full; near one means requests were waiting on the server rather than on the generator, and occupancy_samples is how many samples that fraction rests on.

It stops sending once one further measurement window has passed after the window ends, and missed_in_window counts the scheduled requests that it never sent; a pass with any missed request is not sustained. cap_occupancy is the fraction of the window, sampled off the request path, that the generator spent with its in-flight cap full; near one means requests were waiting on the server rather than on the generator, and occupancy_samples is how many samples that fraction rests on.

It stops sending once one further measurement window has passed after the window ends, and missed_in_window counts the scheduled requests that it never sent; a pass with any missed request is not sustained. cap_occupancy is the fraction of the window, sampled off the request path, that the generator spent with its in-flight cap full; near one means requests were waiting on the server rather than on the generator, and occupancy_samples is how many samples that fraction rests on.

generator.note: offered_fraction is the share of the target rate the generator actually offered, and it is the field to read for whether the load was delivered. It stops sending once one further measurement window has passed after the window ends, and missed_in_window counts the scheduled requests that it never sent; a pass with any missed request is not sustained. cap_occupancy is the fraction of the window, sampled off the request path, that the generator spent with its in-flight cap full; near one means requests were waiting on the server rather than on the generator, and occupancy_samples is how many samples that fraction rests on.

It stops sending once one further measurement window has passed after the window ends, and missed_in_window counts the scheduled requests that it never sent; a pass with any missed request is not sustained. cap_occupancy is the fraction of the window, sampled off the request path, that the generator spent with its in-flight cap full; near one means requests were waiting on the server rather than on the generator, and occupancy_samples is how many samples that fraction rests on.

engine_cpu.note: cores_used is the engine cgroup's cpu.stat usage divided by wall time over the measured span, so it is the average number of cores the engine kept busy, not a peak.

failures.note: A shed failure is the server refusing work to protect itself, not a defect: a rate whose failures are all shed measured a server holding its limit. total counts every failure across all passes at this rate, while the error_rate beside it is one pass’s median, so the two are not comparable.

client_saturation.client: node-postgres (pg) over a pooled binary socket
client_saturation.interpretation: This ceiling is measured on the probe statement above, whose response is a few bytes. A workload returning real rows costs the client more per operation, so its true ceiling is lower than this figure by an amount the probe cannot measure. Read it as an upper bound on the client only: a workload reaching this rate is at the client's limit, while a workload falling below it proves nothing on its own. Whether the server saturated is decided per rate from the generator's in-flight occupancy, not from this number, and headroom_factor is therefore an optimistic bound rather than proof of headroom. Occupancy in turn shows that the generator was waiting on replies rather than failing to send them; separating a server too busy to answer from a client too slow to read the answers needs the same offered load split across several generator processes, which this harness does not run, so a server_saturated verdict rests on occupancy rather than on that stronger test.

network.note: Each sample is the time from opening a TCP connection to a port on the engine's machine until the connection is established, which takes one network round trip. The port belongs to a small service outside the engine, so the probe costs the engine nothing, and the load generator takes the samples before the pass starts.
